blocks.text: DEMOLITION ACROSS PORT PERRY & ALL OF SCUGOG
★★★★★ 700+ Five-Star Reviews on Google
Three Very Different Kinds of Demolition, Priced the Same Way

c: Ask what a typical Port Perry demolition job looks like and the honest answer is: it depends where in the township you’re standing. In old Port Perry’s Victorian streets, it’s usually a shed or a small deck that’s outlived a century-old house — something torn down carefully enough that nobody would guess a demolition crew had even been there. Out on Scugog Island and the waterfront lanes, it’s a dock-adjacent deck or an old above ground pool near the shoreline, cleared with the kind of attention that low ground and close-by water actually demand. And across the concessions toward Blackstock, Nestleton, Seagrave and Greenbank, it’s fence lines and outbuildings that came with a farm property, torn down and hauled off without a distance charge tacked on for how far the address sits from town. Three different jobs, one flat pricing structure — the 700+ five-star reviews behind Live Junk Free reflect that consistency more than anything else.

blocks.text: DEMOLITION FAQ
Demolition Services in Port Perry — Restoration Questions, Honest Answers

items.q: How much does demolition cost in Port Perry?
a: One flat written figure per project, scoped free at your property, covering labour, tear-out, loading, trucking and all disposal — identical math town-wide and township-wide, with no heritage, scenic or distance premium anywhere in it. The approved number holds to the invoice.

items.q: Is there really no extra charge for Scugog Island or waterfront demolition?
a: None. The same flat pricing applies at a Queen Street backyard and at the end of an island lane — no distance fee, no access charge, no seasonal surcharge.

items.q: How careful are you around a heritage building?
a: Very. Original trim, foundations and features that stay get masked and protected before anything comes down, and the work moves at the pace century buildings deserve.

items.q: Can you demolish a deck or structure near the water?
a: Yes, regularly. Docksides, shoreline decking and ground conditions near the water all get accounted for at the walkthrough, with scheduling flexible around the quieter season if you’d prefer.

items.q: Do you handle fence and shed demolition on farm properties toward Blackstock or Nestleton?
a: Yes — long fence runs and multiple farm structures are common work for us, priced the same flat way as a single village backyard job.
